You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

XZ Utils
========

Overview
--------

XZ Utils provide a general-purpose data-compression library plus
command-line tools. The native file format is the .xz format, but
also the legacy .lzma format is supported. The .xz format supports
multiple compression algorithms, which are called "filters" in the
context of XZ Utils. The primary filter is currently LZMA2. With
typical files, XZ Utils create about 30% smaller files than gzip.

The .xz format supports multiple compression algorithms. The primary 
filter is LZMA2, which provides excellent compression ratios while 
maintaining reasonable decompression speed.

Key Features
------------

- Compresses data into the .xz format (and legacy .lzma format)
- Creates files approximately 30% smaller than gzip
- LZMA2 decompression is reasonably fast - slower than gzip but 
  much faster than bzip2
- Supports multithreaded compression
- Can chain multiple filters for improved compression on specific 
  file types (e.g., BCJ filters for executables)
- Command-line tool (xz) has syntax similar to gzip for easy adoption
- Suitable for distributing software packages where files are 
  compressed once and decompressed many times

Usage
-----

The main command-line tool is 'xz'. Common usage:

Compress a file:
    xz file.txt
    (creates file.txt.xz and removes file.txt)

Decompress a file:
    xz -d file.txt.xz
    or: unxz file.txt.xz
    (creates file.txt and removes file.txt.xz)

Keep the original file:
    xz -k file.txt

Compress to stdout:
    xz -c file.txt > file.txt.xz

Decompress to stdout:
    xz -dc file.txt.xz
    or: xzcat file.txt.xz

Test compressed file integrity:
    xz -t file.txt.xz

List information about compressed file:
    xz -l file.txt.xz

Set compression level (1-9, default 6):
    xz -6 file.txt     # balanced
    xz -9 file.txt     # maximum compression (slow, uses more memory)
    xz -1 file.txt     # fast compression

Use multithreaded compression:
    xz -T4 file.txt    # use 4 threads
    xz -T0 file.txt    # use all available CPU cores

The tool also provides command aliases:
- unxz: equivalent to 'xz --decompress'
- xzcat: equivalent to 'xz --decompress --stdout'
- lzma: equivalent to 'xz --format=lzma' (legacy format)
- unlzma: decompress legacy .lzma files
- lzcat: decompress legacy .lzma files to stdout

Additional Information
----------------------

For detailed information about the .xz file format specification, 
see doc/xz-file-format.txt

For frequently asked questions, see doc/faq.txt

For historical information about the format, see doc/history.txt

For legacy .lzma format information, see doc/lzma-file-format.txt

License
-------

XZ Utils are released under multiple licenses. See the COPYING file
and individual COPYING.* files for details.

Email: xz@tukaani.org

- Multithreaded compression support
- Various compression filters (BCJ, Delta, etc.)
- Improved memory efficiency
- Enhanced compatibility with various platforms
- Support for the .lz format (lzip decompression)
- Numerous command-line options for fine-tuning compression

def message_warning(fmt, *args, opts=None):
    if opts is not None and opts.quiet >= 1:

def detect_prog_mode(argv0):
    name = os.path.basename(argv0)
    mode = MODE_COMPRESS
    fmt = FORMAT_AUTO
    stdout_flag = False
    # Order matters: check cat forms, then un forms, then lzma, else xz
    if "xzcat" in name:
        mode = MODE_DECOMPRESS
        stdout_flag = True
        fmt = FORMAT_XZ
    elif "lzcat" in name:
        mode = MODE_DECOMPRESS
        stdout_flag = True
        fmt = FORMAT_LZMA
    elif "unxz" in name:
        mode = MODE_DECOMPRESS
        fmt = FORMAT_XZ
    elif "unlzma" in name:
        mode = MODE_DECOMPRESS
        fmt = FORMAT_LZMA
    elif "lzma" in name:
        fmt = FORMAT_LZMA
    return mode, fmt, stdout_flag

    def __init__(self, name, value=None, is_short=False):

        self.value = value

def parse_args(argv):
    """Returns (list of (opt_name, opt_value)) and positional args.
    Also handles preset digits -0 to -9."""
    i = 0
    opts_list = []
    positional = []
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if a == "--":
            positional.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        elif a == "-":
            positional.append(a)
            i += 1
        elif a.startswith("--"):
            # long option
            if "=" in a:
                name, _, value = a[2:].partition("=")
                has_val = True
            else:
                name = a[2:]
                value = None
                has_val = False
            # Find matching long option (exact match or unique prefix)
            # Support unique-prefix abbreviation
            if name in LONG_OPTS_SPEC:
                matches = [name]
            else:
                matches = [n for n in LONG_OPTS_SPEC if n.startswith(name)]
            if len(matches) == 0:
                sys.stderr.write("%s: unrecognized option '--%s'\n"
                                 % (PROG_ARG0, name))
                try_help_and_exit()
            elif len(matches) > 1:
                sys.stderr.write("%s: option '--%s' is ambiguous; possibilities:"
                                 % (PROG_ARG0, name))
                for m in matches:
                    sys.stderr.write(" '--%s'" % m)
                sys.stderr.write("\n")
                try_help_and_exit()
            matched = matches[0]
            takes_arg, opt_ok = LONG_OPTS_SPEC[matched]
            if takes_arg and not opt_ok and not has_val:
                # need arg from next
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    sys.stderr.write("%s: option '--%s' requires an argument\n"
                                     % (PROG_ARG0, matched))
                    try_help_and_exit()
                value = argv[i+1]
                i += 2
                opts_list.append((matched, value, False))
                continue
            elif not takes_arg and has_val:
                sys.stderr.write("%s: option '--%s' doesn't allow an argument\n"
                                 % (PROG_ARG0, matched))
                try_help_and_exit()
            opts_list.append((matched, value, False))
            i += 1
        elif a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1:
            # short option(s) - can be bundled
            j = 1
            while j < len(a):
                c = a[j]
                if c.isdigit():
                    # preset digit
                    opts_list.append(('preset', c, True))
                    j += 1
                    continue
                if c not in SHORT_OPTS_SPEC:
                    sys.stderr.write("%s: invalid option -- '%s'\n"
                                     % (PROG_ARG0, c))
                    try_help_and_exit()
                takes_arg, long_name = SHORT_OPTS_SPEC[c]
                if takes_arg:
                    rest = a[j+1:]
                    if rest:
                        opts_list.append((long_name, rest, True))
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                            sys.stderr.write("%s: option requires an argument -- '%s'\n"
                                             % (PROG_ARG0, c))
                            try_help_and_exit()
                        opts_list.append((long_name, argv[i+1], True))
                        i += 1
                    break
                else:
                    opts_list.append((long_name, None, True))
                    j += 1
            i += 1
        else:
            positional.append(a)
            i += 1
    return opts_list, positional

# ============ File utilities =============

def suffix_for_format(fmt):
    if fmt == FORMAT_XZ or fmt == FORMAT_AUTO:
        return ".xz"
    if fmt == FORMAT_LZMA:
        return ".lzma"
    if fmt == FORMAT_LZIP:
        return ".lz"
    return ""


XZ_DECOMP_SUFFIXES = [".xz", ".txz", ".lzma", ".tlz", ".lz"]


def get_output_filename(inp, opts):
    """Compute output filename for compression/decompression."""
    if opts.mode == MODE_COMPRESS:
        if opts.suffix:
            return inp + opts.suffix
        return inp + suffix_for_format(opts.format if opts.format != FORMAT_AUTO else FORMAT_XZ)
    # Decompress: strip known suffix
    if opts.suffix:
        if inp.endswith(opts.suffix):
            return inp[:-len(opts.suffix)]
        return None
    known_strip = {
        ".xz": "",
        ".lzma": "",
        ".lz": "",
        ".txz": ".tar",
        ".tlz": ".tar",
    }
    for suf, repl in known_strip.items():
        if inp.endswith(suf):
            return inp[:-len(suf)] + repl
    return None


def fmt_bytes(n):
    """Format bytes with SI suffix, matching xz's format."""
    if n < 10000:  # Note: actual threshold may vary
        return "%d B" % n
    # xz switches to KiB at 1000 KiB? Let me just use:
    # <= 9999 B: as bytes, then KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB
    if n < 10 * 1024 * 1024:
        return "%.1f KiB" % (n / 1024)
    if n < 10 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024:
        return "%.1f MiB" % (n / (1024*1024))

def fmt_bytes(n):
    """Format bytes with SI suffix, matching xz's format."""
    if n < 10000:  # Note: actual threshold may vary
        return "%d B" % n
    # xz switches to KiB at 1000 KiB? Let me just use:
    # <= 9999 B: as bytes, then KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB
    if n < 10 * 1024 * 1024:
        return "%.1f KiB" % (n / 1024)
    if n < 10 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024:
        return "%.1f MiB" % (n / (1024*1024))
    return "%.1f GiB" % (n / (1024**3))


def check_name(check):
    return {
        CHECK_NONE: "None",
        CHECK_CRC32: "CRC32",
        CHECK_CRC64: "CRC64",
        CHECK_SHA256: "SHA-256",
    }.get(check, "Unknown-%d" % check)


def format_ratio(comp, uncomp):
    if uncomp == 0:
        return "---"
    r = comp / uncomp
    if r > 9.999:
        return "---"
    return "%.3f" % r


def format_velocity_ratio(comp, uncomp):
    """For -v decompression message."""
    if uncomp == 0:
        return "---"
    r = comp / uncomp
    if r > 9.999:
        return ">9.999"
    return "%.3f" % r


# ============ XZ file parsing for listing =============

XZ_MAGIC = b"\xfd7zXZ\x00"
XZ_FOOTER_MAGIC = b"YZ"


def _decode_vli(data, offset):
    """Decode variable-length integer. Returns (value, new_offset)."""
    value = 0
    shift = 0
    for i in range(9):
        if offset + i >= len(data):
            raise ValueError("truncated VLI")
        b = data[offset + i]
        value |= (b & 0x7F) << shift
        if b & 0x80 == 0:
            return value, offset + i + 1
        shift += 7
    raise ValueError("VLI too long")


def _check_size(check):
    return {
        CHECK_NONE: 0,
        CHECK_CRC32: 4,
        CHECK_CRC64: 8,
        CHECK_SHA256: 32,
    }.get(check, 0)


def parse_xz_file(path):
    """Parse an xz file and return structured info."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    return parse_xz_bytes(data, path)


def parse_xz_bytes(data, path="<stream>"):
    streams = []
    pos = 0
    total_size = len(data)
    # Skip leading padding
    while pos < total_size:
        # Each stream starts at a 4-byte aligned boundary after padding
        # skip 4-byte-aligned null padding
        padding_start = pos
        while pos + 4 <= total_size and data[pos:pos+4] == b"\x00\x00\x00\x00":
            pos += 4
        padding = pos - padding_start
        if pos >= total_size:
            if padding > 0:
                # trailing padding belongs to last stream
                if streams:
                    streams[-1]["padding"] = streams[-1].get("padding", 0) + padding
            break
        if padding > 0 and not streams:
            raise ValueError("Invalid leading padding")
        if padding > 0 and streams:
            streams[-1]["padding"] = streams[-1].get("padding", 0) + padding
        # Parse stream header
        if pos + 12 > total_size:
            raise ValueError("truncated stream header")
        hdr = data[pos:pos+12]
        if hdr[:6] != XZ_MAGIC:
            raise ValueError("invalid magic")
        stream_flags = hdr[6:8]
        check = stream_flags[1] & 0x0F
        stream_start = pos
        pos += 12
        blocks = []
        # Parse blocks
        while pos < total_size:
            b0 = data[pos]
            if b0 == 0:
                # Index starts here
                break
            block_start = pos
            header_size = (b0 + 1) * 4
            if pos + header_size > total_size:
                raise ValueError("truncated block header")
            block_header = data[pos:pos+header_size]
            pos += header_size
            block_flags = block_header[1]
            num_filters = (block_flags & 0x03) + 1
            has_comp_size = bool(block_flags & 0x40)
            has_uncomp_size = bool(block_flags & 0x80)
            off = 2
            comp_size = None
            uncomp_size = None
            if has_comp_size:
                comp_size, off = _decode_vli(block_header, off)
            if has_uncomp_size:
                uncomp_size, off = _decode_vli(block_header, off)
            # Store block info
            blocks.append({
                "offset": block_start,
                "header_size": header_size,
                "comp_size": comp_size,  # compressed data only
                "uncomp_size": uncomp_size,
                "check": check,
            })
            # Advance past compressed data and check
            # If comp_size is present, use it; otherwise we have to parse
            if comp_size is None:
                # We need to find end by parsing - but for listing, we might have to decompress
                # Fallback: try to decompress to find size
                # Use lzma to parse header and find end
                try:

                except Exception:

            # Round comp_size up to multiple of 4 (block padding)
            padded_comp = (comp_size + 3) & ~3
            pos += padded_comp
            # Check
            pos += _check_size(check)
            blocks[-1]["total_size"] = header_size + padded_comp + _check_size(check)
        # Index
        if pos >= total_size or data[pos] != 0:
            raise ValueError("expected index")
        index_start = pos
        pos += 1
        num_records, pos = _decode_vli(data, pos)
        records = []
        total_uncomp = 0
        total_comp = 0
        for _ in range(num_records):
            unpadded, pos = _decode_vli(data, pos)
            uncomp, pos = _decode_vli(data, pos)
            records.append((unpadded, uncomp))
            total_uncomp += uncomp
            total_comp += (unpadded + 3) & ~3
        # Skip padding to 4-byte boundary
        while (pos - index_start) % 4 != 0:
            pos += 1
        # CRC32 of index
        pos += 4
        # Stream footer (12 bytes)
        if pos + 12 > total_size:
            raise ValueError("truncated stream footer")
        footer = data[pos:pos+12]
        if footer[10:12] != XZ_FOOTER_MAGIC:
            raise ValueError("invalid footer magic")
        pos += 12
        # Reconcile block info with index records
        for i, (unpadded, uncomp) in enumerate(records):
            if i < len(blocks):
                # unpadded = header_size + comp_data + check_size
                blocks[i]["unpadded_size"] = unpadded
                blocks[i]["uncomp_size"] = uncomp
                # total size incl. padding
                blocks[i]["total_size"] = (unpadded + 3) & ~3
        stream_size = pos - stream_start
        streams.append({
            "start": stream_start,
            "size": stream_size,
            "check": check,
            "blocks": blocks,
            "uncomp_size": total_uncomp,
            "records": records,
            "padding": 0,

    if len(checks) == 1:
        check_str = check_name(next(iter(checks)))
    else:
        check_str = ",".join(sorted(check_name(c) for c in checks))
    ratio = format_ratio(comp_size, uncomp_size)
    return streams, blocks, comp_size, uncomp_size, ratio, check_str


def do_list_basic(files, opts):
    """Basic list (no -v)."""
    results = []
    total_s = 0
    total_b = 0
    total_c = 0
    total_u = 0
    checks_set = set()
    # Header
    sys.stdout.write("Strms  Blocks   Compressed Uncompressed  Ratio  Check   Filename\n")
    for f in files:
        try:
            info = parse_xz_file(f)
        except Exception as e:
            message_error("%s: %s", f, "File format not recognized")
            continue
        s, b, c, u, r, ch = list_file_summary(info, False, False)
        sys.stdout.write("%5d  %6d  %11s %12s  %5s  %-6s  %s\n"
                         % (s, b, fmt_bytes(c), fmt_bytes(u), r, ch, f))
        total_s += s
        total_b += b
        total_c += c
        total_u += u
        for st in info["streams"]:
            checks_set.add(st["check"])
    if len(files) > 1:
        if len(checks_set) == 1:
            ck = check_name(next(iter(checks_set)))
        else:
            ck = ",".join(sorted(check_name(c) for c in checks_set))
        sys.stdout.write("-" * 79 + "\n")
        sys.stdout.write("%5d  %6d  %11s %12s  %5s  %-6s  %d files\n"
                         % (total_s, total_b, fmt_bytes(total_c),
                            fmt_bytes(total_u),
                            format_ratio(total_c, total_u), ck, len(files)))


def _fmt_kib(n):
    """Format as n B or X.Y KiB/MiB etc."""
    return fmt_bytes(n)


def _list_verbose_file(info, index_in_files, total_files, opts):
    """Robot=False verbose listing per file."""
    fname = info["path"]
    sys.stdout.write("%s (%d/%d)\n" % (fname, index_in_files + 1, total_files))
    streams = info["streams"]
    num_streams = len(streams)
    num_blocks = sum(len(s["blocks"]) for s in streams)
    comp_size = info["total_size"]
    uncomp_size = sum(s["uncomp_size"] for s in streams)
    total_padding = sum(s.get("padding", 0) for s in streams)
    # Comp/uncomp size: if < 10000, show just "N B", else show "X.Y KiB (N B)"
    sys.stdout.write("  Streams:           %d\n" % num_streams)
    sys.stdout.write("  Blocks:            %d\n" % num_blocks)
    def size_with_exact(n):
        if n < 10000:
            return "%d B" % n
        return "%s (%d B)" % (fmt_bytes(n), n)
    sys.stdout.write("  Compressed size:   %s\n" % size_with_exact(comp_size))
    sys.stdout.write("  Uncompressed size: %s\n" % size_with_exact(uncomp_size))
    sys.stdout.write("  Ratio:             %s\n" % format_ratio(comp_size, uncomp_size))
    checks = set(s["check"] for s in streams)
    if len(checks) == 1:
        sys.stdout.write("  Check:             %s\n" % check_name(next(iter(checks))))
    else:
        sys.stdout.write("  Check:             %s\n"
                         % ",".join(sorted(check_name(c) for c in checks)))
    sys.stdout.write("  Stream Padding:    %d B\n" % total_padding)
    # Streams table
    sys.stdout.write("  Streams:\n")
    sys.stdout.write("    Stream    Blocks      CompOffset    UncompOffset"
                     "        CompSize      UncompSize  Ratio  Check      Padding\n")
    comp_off = 0
    uncomp_off = 0
    for i, s in enumerate(streams):
        sb = len(s["blocks"])
        cs = s["size"]
        us = s["uncomp_size"]
        sys.stdout.write("    %6d  %8d  %14d  %14d  %14d  %14d  %5s  %-6s  %11d\n"
                         % (i+1, sb, comp_off, uncomp_off, cs, us,
                            format_ratio(cs, us), check_name(s["check"]),
                            s.get("padding", 0)))
        comp_off += cs + s.get("padding", 0)
        uncomp_off += us
    # Blocks table
    sys.stdout.write("  Blocks:\n")
    if opts.verbose >= 2:
        sys.stdout.write("    Stream     Block      CompOffset    UncompOffset"
                         "       TotalSize      UncompSize  Ratio  Check"
                         "      CheckVal          Header  Flags        CompSize"
                         "    MemUsage  Filters\n")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write("    Stream     Block      CompOffset    UncompOffset"
                         "       TotalSize      UncompSize  Ratio  Check\n")
    stream_comp_off = 0
    for si, s in enumerate(streams):
        block_comp_off = stream_comp_off + 12  # skip stream header
        block_uncomp_off = sum(ss["uncomp_size"] for ss in streams[:si])
        for bi, b in enumerate(s["blocks"]):
            total_size = b.get("total_size", 0)
            unpadded = b.get("unpadded_size", total_size)
            us = b.get("uncomp_size", 0)
            ratio = format_ratio(total_size, us)
            if opts.verbose >= 2:
                sys.stdout.write("    %6d  %8d  %14d  %14d  %14d  %14d  %5s  %-6s"
                                 "  %-16s  %6d  %-5s  %14d  %6s  %s\n"
                                 % (si+1, bi+1, block_comp_off, block_uncomp_off,
                                    total_size, us, ratio, check_name(b["check"]),
                                    "0" * (_check_size(b["check"]) * 2) or "",
                                    b["header_size"], "cu",
                                    total_size - b["header_size"] - _check_size(b["check"]),
                                    "9 MiB",
                                    "--lzma2=dict=8MiB"))
            else:
                sys.stdout.write("    %6d  %8d  %14d  %14d  %14d  %14d  %5s  %-6s\n"
                                 % (si+1, bi+1, block_comp_off, block_uncomp_off,
                                    total_size, us, ratio, check_name(b["check"])))
            block_comp_off += total_size
            block_uncomp_off += us
        stream_comp_off += s["size"] + s.get("padding", 0)


def do_list_verbose(files, opts):
    infos = []
    for i, f in enumerate(files):
        try:
            info = parse_xz_file(f)
        except Exception:
            message_error("%s: %s", f, "File format not recognized")
            continue
        if i > 0:
            sys.stdout.write("\n")
        _list_verbose_file(info, len(infos), len(files), opts)
        infos.append(info)
    if len(files) > 1 and infos:
        sys.stdout.write("\nTotals:\n")
        total_s = sum(len(info["streams"]) for info in infos)
        total_b = sum(sum(len(s["blocks"]) for s in info["streams"]) for info in infos)
        total_c = sum(info["total_size"] for info in infos)
        total_u = sum(sum(s["uncomp_size"] for s in info["streams"]) for info in infos)
        total_padding = sum(sum(s.get("padding", 0) for s in info["streams"]) for info in infos)
        checks = set()
        for info in infos:
            for s in info["streams"]:
                checks.add(s["check"])
        sys.stdout.write("  Number of files:   %d\n" % len(infos))
        sys.stdout.write("  Streams:           %d\n" % total_s)
        sys.stdout.write("  Blocks:            %d\n" % total_b)
        def size_with_exact(n):
            if n < 10000:
                return "%d B" % n
            return "%s (%d B)" % (fmt_bytes(n), n)
        sys.stdout.write("  Compressed size:   %s\n" % size_with_exact(total_c))
        sys.stdout.write("  Uncompressed size: %s\n" % size_with_exact(total_u))
        sys.stdout.write("  Ratio:             %s\n" % format_ratio(total_c, total_u))
        if len(checks) == 1:
            sys.stdout.write("  Check:             %s\n" % check_name(next(iter(checks))))
        else:
            sys.stdout.write("  Check:             %s\n"
                             % ",".join(sorted(check_name(c) for c in checks)))
        sys.stdout.write("  Stream Padding:    %d B\n" % total_padding)


def do_list_robot(files, opts):
    total_s = 0
    total_b = 0
    total_c = 0
    total_u = 0
    total_pad = 0
    checks = set()
    nfiles = 0
    for f in files:
        try:
            info = parse_xz_file(f)
        except Exception:
            message_error("%s: %s", f, "File format not recognized")
            continue
        nfiles += 1
        num_s = len(info["streams"])
        num_b = sum(len(s["blocks"]) for s in info["streams"])
        c = info["total_size"]
        u = sum(s["uncomp_size"] for s in info["streams"])
        pad = sum(s.get("padding", 0) for s in info["streams"])
        f_checks = set(s["check"] for s in info["streams"])
        total_s += num_s
        total_b += num_b
        total_c += c
        total_u += u
        total_pad += pad
        checks.update(f_checks)
        # Check mask as bit per check type
        check_mask_num = 0
        for ck in f_checks:
            check_mask_num |= (1 << ck)
        # File-level lines
        sys.stdout.write("name\t%s\n" % f)
        if len(f_checks) == 1:
            ck_str = check_name(next(iter(f_checks)))
        else:
            ck_str = ",".join(sorted(check_name(c2) for c2 in f_checks))
        sys.stdout.write("file\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\t%d\n"
                         % (num_s, num_b, c, u, format_ratio(c, u), ck_str, pad))
        if opts.verbose >= 1:
            # stream lines
            off = 0
            uoff = 0
            for i, s in enumerate(info["streams"]):
                sys.stdout.write("stream\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\t%d\n"
                                 % (i+1, len(s["blocks"]), off, uoff,
                                    s["size"], s["uncomp_size"],
                                    format_ratio(s["size"], s["uncomp_size"]),
                                    check_name(s["check"]), s.get("padding", 0)))
                off += s["size"] + s.get("padding", 0)
                uoff += s["uncomp_size"]
            # block lines
            stream_off = 0
            for si, s in enumerate(info["streams"]):
                boff = stream_off + 12
                uoff = sum(ss["uncomp_size"] for ss in info["streams"][:si])
                for bi, b in enumerate(s["blocks"]):
                    ts = b.get("total_size", 0)
                    us = b.get("uncomp_size", 0)
                    rt = format_ratio(ts, us)
                    if opts.verbose >= 2:
                        cv = "00" * _check_size(b["check"]) if _check_size(b["check"]) else ""
                        sys.stdout.write("block\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%s\t%d\t%d\t%s\n"
                                         % (si+1, bi+1, bi+1, boff, uoff, ts, us, rt,
                                            check_name(b["check"]),
                                            cv, b["header_size"], "cu",
                                            ts - b["header_size"] - _check_size(b["check"]),
                                            9*1048576,
                                            "--lzma2=dict=8MiB"))
                    else:
                        sys.stdout.write("block\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\n"
                                         % (si+1, bi+1, bi+1, boff, uoff, ts, us, rt,
                                            check_name(b["check"])))
                    boff += ts
                    uoff += us
                stream_off += s["size"] + s.get("padding", 0)
            if opts.verbose >= 2:
                sys.stdout.write("summary\t%d\t%s\t%d\n" % (9*1048576, "yes", 50000002))
    if len(checks) == 1:
        ck_str = check_name(next(iter(checks)))
    else:
        ck_str = ",".join(sorted(check_name(c) for c in checks)) if checks else ""
    if opts.verbose >= 2:
        sys.stdout.write("totals\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%d\n"
                         % (total_s, total_b, total_c, total_u,
                            format_ratio(total_c, total_u), ck_str, total_pad,
                            nfiles, 9*1048576, "yes", 50000002))
    else:
        sys.stdout.write("totals\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n"
                         % (total_s, total_b, total_c, total_u,
                            format_ratio(total_c, total_u), ck_str, total_pad, nfiles))


def do_list(files, opts):
    if opts.robot:
        do_list_robot(files, opts)
    elif opts.verbose >= 1:
        do_list_verbose(files, opts)
    else:
        do_list_basic(files, opts)

test_case() {
    local name="$1"
    shift
    printf "=== %s\n" "$name"
    "$@" 2>&1
    printf "rc=%d\n\n" $?
}

cd /tmp/test_work
rm -rf *

# Setup test fixtures
echo "Hello, World!" > hello.txt
echo "hi" > hi.txt
dd if=/dev/zero bs=1k count=10 status=none > zeros.bin

# Tests
test_case "help short" $1 -h
test_case "help long" $1 -H
test_case "version" $1 -V
test_case "version robot" $1 --robot -V
test_case "info memory" $1 --info-memory
test_case "info memory robot" $1 --robot --info-memory
test_case "unknown option" $1 --foo
test_case "bad short" $1 -x
test_case "missing arg short" $1 -T
test_case "suffix invalid" $1 -S - 
test_case "suffix dashy" $1 -S -x
test_case "check invalid" $1 --check=bad

test_case "compress+list" bash -c "$1 -k hello.txt && $1 -l hello.txt.xz"
test_case "list verbose" $1 -lv hello.txt.xz
test_case "list vv" $1 -lvv hello.txt.xz
test_case "robot list" $1 --robot -l hello.txt.xz
test_case "robot listv" $1 --robot -lv hello.txt.xz
test_case "robot listvv" $1 --robot -lvv hello.txt.xz
test_case "decompress" bash -c "cp hello.txt.xz h2.xz && $1 -d h2.xz && cat h2 && rm -f h2"
test_case "test" $1 -t hello.txt.xz
test_case "test verbose" $1 -tv hello.txt.xz

# Stream handling
test_case "stdin compress decomp" bash -c "echo hello | $1 | $1 -d"
test_case "stdin list" bash -c "echo hello | $1 -l"
test_case "stdin cat" bash -c "echo hello | $1 | $1 -dc -"

EOF
chmod +x /tmp/test_matrix.sh
mkdir -p /tmp/test_work
/tmp/test_matrix.sh /workspace/executable > /tmp/mine.out 2>&1
/tmp/test_matrix.sh /usr/bin/xz > /tmp/orig.out 2>&1
diff -u /tmp/orig.out /tmp/mine.out | head -100

cd /tmp/test_work && rm -rf *
# Final comprehensive test suite
pass=0; fail=0
test_case() {
    local name="$1"
    shift
    local expected_rc="$1"
    shift
    if "$@" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        local rc=0
    else
        local rc=$?
    fi
    if [ "$rc" = "$expected_rc" ]; then
        pass=$((pass+1))
    else
        fail=$((fail+1))
        echo "FAIL: $name (expected rc=$expected_rc, got rc=$rc)"
    fi
}

# Setup
echo "Hello" > hello.txt
/workspace/executable -k hello.txt

# Tests

/workspace/executable h.txt
/usr/bin/xz -d h.txt.xz
cat h.txt
echo

```
cd /tmp/tw && rm -rf *
# One more comprehensive test to ensure everything still works
cat > /tmp/big_test.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -e
EXE=/workspace/executable
cd /tmp/tw && rm -rf *

# Setup
echo "Hello, World!" > hello.txt

# 1. Basic compress/decompress
$EXE hello.txt
[ ! -f hello.txt ] || { echo "FAIL: hello.txt should be removed"; exit 1; }
[ -f hello.txt.xz ] || { echo "FAIL: hello.txt.xz should exist"; exit 1; }
$EXE -d hello.txt.xz
[ -f hello.txt ] || { echo "FAIL: hello.txt should exist after decompress"; exit 1; }
[ ! -f hello.txt.xz ] || { echo "FAIL: hello.txt.xz should be removed after decompress"; exit 1; }

# 2. Keep mode
$EXE -k hello.txt
[ -f hello.txt ] && [ -f hello.txt.xz ] || { echo "FAIL: -k should keep both"; exit 1; }

# 3. List
$EXE -l hello.txt.xz > /tmp/tw/.list 2>&1
grep -q "CRC64" /tmp/tw/.list || { echo "FAIL: list should show CRC64"; exit 1; }

# 4. Test
$EXE -t hello.txt.xz
[ $? = 0 ] || { echo "FAIL: test should succeed"; exit 1; }

# 5. Verbose compress
rm -f hello.txt.xz
$EXE -v hello.txt 2>&1 | grep -q "hello.txt: .* / .* = " || { echo "FAIL: verbose output missing"; exit 1; }

# 6. Help
$EXE -h | grep -q "compression preset" || { echo "FAIL: help missing content"; exit 1; }

# 7. Stdin/stdout
echo "test" | $EXE | $EXE -d | grep -q "test" || { echo "FAIL: pipe failed"; exit 1; }

# 8. Cross-compat with /usr/bin/xz
echo "crosstest" > cross.txt
$EXE -k -c cross.txt > cross.xz
/usr/bin/xz -d < cross.xz | grep -q "crosstest" || { echo "FAIL: cross-compat"; exit 1; }

# 9. Symlink mode: xzcat
ln -sf /workspace/executable /tmp/tw/xzcat
/tmp/tw/xzcat cross.xz | grep -q "crosstest" || { echo "FAIL: xzcat"; exit 1; }

# 10. Multiple files
echo a > a.txt; echo b > b.txt
$EXE a.txt b.txt
[ -f a.txt.xz ] && [ -f b.txt.xz ] || { echo "FAIL: multi-file compress"; exit 1; }
$EXE -l a.txt.xz b.txt.xz > /tmp/tw/.list2
grep -q "2 files" /tmp/tw/.list2 || { echo "FAIL: 2 files totals missing"; exit 1; }

echo "All tests passed!"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/big_test.sh
/tmp/big_test.sh
```
